note: Every spoken story line in Life of a Worm. Gary voices each id to res://assets/story/voice/<id>.ogg from the speaker's saved voice library (old_reel: Chatterbox library voice; bobber: his library voice once made). Until a file exists the line plays fallback: bark:<cue> is the speaker's library bark, else a short placeholder blip (scripts/story/story_voice.gd: library bark file if vendored, else a synth placeholder babble in the speaker's pitch). text is the script for the voice, never shown in play (subtitles are off by default). [tags] are ElevenLabs v3-style directions. excuse: Reel's reason the worms changed, different every time.

lines.text: Grandpa? Why's a sandwich on my hook? Why not worms?
lines.delivery: curious, a bit put out, quick

lines.text: [chuckles] Worms? Heh. Back in my day, worms were little.
lines.delivery: low, slow, creaky; chuckle first; trails off

lines.text: THIS big. Fit right on a hook...
lines.delivery: holds two fingers an inch apart; fond, quiet

lines.text: That's teeny.
Heh. Then one morning, right here by the pond...
lines.delivery: slows down, story voice, drifting into memory

lines.text: [hums] Come on, little fella. Breakfast for the fish.
lines.delivery: younger, brighter, humming while baiting the hook

lines.text: Two of 'em, come to think of it.
One I called Gulp. The other one... [chuckles] Burp.
lines.delivery: fond, slow; the chuckle lands right before Burp

lines.text: [giggles] BURP!
lines.delivery: delighted kid giggle, then shouts it

lines.text: Heh. That one got away... Well. Those two.
lines.delivery: the old catchphrase, then a sheepish correction, quieter

lines.text: And then... it got HUNGRY.
[chuckles] That worm ate everything smaller than itself.
lines.delivery: proud, like bragging about a grandkid

lines.text: So do I!
lines.delivery: delighted, fist pump, mouth full of sandwich

lines.text: Heh heh. That's my boy.
Seeds. Roots. Bugs. Got THIS big.
lines.delivery: counts on fingers, then hands a hand-width apart

lines.text: Bugs? EWWW.
It wasn't just bigger, see. It was... different.
A worm with a ROCK for a head?
Heh. Must've been that comet. Whoosh! Right over the pond.
lines.delivery: excuse 1: points at the sky, sure of himself

lines.text: Got THIS big, too.
Hmmmm.
Then one day it came UP. Right under my shed...
lines.delivery: building; keeps talking while the shed sinks behind him

lines.text: Heh. Your grandma's chili, I reckon. Fed it one spoonful.
It was THIS big!
Nuh-uh.
Honest! Never saw that shed again.
lines.delivery: wounded dignity, hand on heart, trails off

lines.text: Nobody fished that year. Whole town watched the hill.
Ho ho! Look at it GO!
lines.delivery: the only delighted one; hops; laughing

lines.text: Dug the bait up by a funny purple rock, see. That's why.
THIS big. Bigger!
lines.delivery: on tiptoe, arms as wide as a hug

lines.text: Nuh-UH.
[chuckles] It was THIS... big.
lines.delivery: arms as wide as they go; strains

lines.text: Ate my lucky socks first. Powerful socks, those.
And then it ate... everything.
Then where are WE sitting?
...It's a long story.
Too big for the ground, so... up it went.
Lightning hit it on the nose. Zap! That's why.
Worms can't fly, Grandpa.
lines.delivery: patient, like explaining to a baby

lines.text: Heh. Didn't say fly. Said UP.
Hmmmm... nuh-uh.
lines.delivery: the squint: one eye closed, slow and sceptical

lines.text: Heh. And it's still out there. Eating stars.
Maybe it was my wish. I wished for the big one.
Nuh... uh...
Never did catch it. Glad I didn't.
lines.delivery: whisper, smile in the voice, trails off

lines.text: Then what, Grandpa? It ate the SUN! What's left?
lines.delivery: wide awake again, sitting up, amazed

lines.text: [chuckles] What's left? A new tin, that's what. Fresh dirt, a whole new world in it.
lines.delivery: pleased with himself, slow, taps the lid

lines.text: And a worm that big always keeps one little thing from last time. You pick which.
Again! Tell it again!
